sentences.zh: 蓋婦人之德，雖在於溫柔，立節垂名，咸資於貞烈。

translations.literal: For a woman's virtue, although it lies in gentleness, to establish integrity and leave a name depends entirely on chastity and fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's virtue may rest in gentleness, yet to establish her integrity and win lasting renown she must draw on chastity and fortitude.

sentences.zh: 溫柔仁之本也，貞烈義之資也。

translations.literal: Gentleness is the root of benevolence; chastity and fortitude are the resources of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleness is the foundation of benevolence, and chastity and fortitude are what give righteousness its force.

sentences.zh: 非溫柔無以成其仁，非貞烈無以顯其義。

translations.literal: Without gentleness one cannot complete benevolence; without chastity and fortitude one cannot display righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Without gentleness benevolence cannot be fulfilled; without chastity and fortitude righteousness cannot be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 是以《詩書》所記，風俗所存，圖像丹青，流聲竹素。

translations.literal: Therefore what the Odes and Documents record, what custom preserves, what paintings depict, and what fame transmits on bamboo and silk—
translations.idiomatic: What the Odes and Documents record, what custom preserves, what painters set down in color, and what fame carries on bamboo and silk—

sentences.zh: 莫不守約以居正，殺身以成仁者也。

translations.literal: all are none other than those who kept their pledges to dwell in rectitude and gave their lives to fulfill benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: all alike are women who kept their vows and lived uprightly, who gave their lives to fulfill the demands of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 若文伯、王陵之母，白公、杞殖之妻，魯之義姑，梁之高行，衛君靈王之妾，夏侯文寧之女，或抱信以會真，或蹈忠而踐義，不以存亡易心，不以盛衰改節，其佳名彰於既沒，徽音傳於不朽，不亦休乎！

translations.literal: Such as the mothers of Wen Bo and Wang Ling, the wives of Duke Bai and Qi Zhi, the righteous aunt of Lu, the lofty conduct of Liang, the concubine of Duke Ling of Wei, and the daughter of Xiahou Wenning—some embraced faith to meet truth, some trod loyalty to practice righteousness; they did not change their hearts for life or death, nor alter their integrity for prosperity or decline. Their fine names shine after death; their excellent reputations pass to immortality—is this not splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Think of the mothers of Wen Bo and Wang Ling, the wives of Duke Bai and Qi Zhi, the righteous aunt of Lu, the woman of lofty conduct in Liang, the concubine of Duke Ling of Wei, and the daughter of Xiahou Wenning: some clung to faith until truth was fulfilled, others walked loyalty into the practice of righteousness. None of them shifted heart with life or death, or changed integrity with fortune's rise and fall. Their fine names blaze after they are gone; their worthy fame lives on undying—is that not glorious?

sentences.zh: 或有王公大人之妃，偶肆情於淫僻之俗，雖衣文衣，食珍膳，坐金屋，乘玉輦，不入彤管之書，不沾青史之筆，將草木以俱落，與麋鹿而同死者，可勝道哉！

translations.literal: Yet there are consorts of kings and great men who occasionally indulge the customs of lewd depravity; though they wear patterned robes, eat rare delicacies, sit in golden chambers, and ride jade carriages, they enter not the red-tube records nor touch the brush of the blue annals—they will fall with the grass and trees and die like elk and deer: can such cases be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: Then there are the consorts of princes and great men who give themselves to corrupt and licentious ways. Though they wear brocade, dine on delicacies, dwell in gilded chambers, and ride in jade carriages, they win no place in the court historians' books and no line in the blue annals. They will wither away with the grass and trees and perish no better than elk in the wild—who could count them all?

sentences.zh: 永言載思，實庶姬之恥也。

translations.literal: To speak of this forever and bear it in mind is truly the shame of common concubines.
translations.idiomatic: To ponder this at length is to grasp the disgrace that awaits any woman who lacks such virtue.

sentences.zh: 《魏》、《隋》二書，並有《列女傳》，《齊》、《周》並無此篇。

translations.literal: The histories of Wei and Sui both have a 'Biographies of Exemplary Women'; those of Qi and Zhou have no such chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The histories of Wei and Sui both include a 'Biographies of Exemplary Women,' whereas those of Qi and Zhou do not.

sentences.zh: 今又得武孫道溫妻趙氏、河北孫神妻陳氏，附《魏》、《隋》二傳，以備《列女篇》云。

translations.literal: Now we have also obtained Zhao, wife of Sun Daowen of Wu, and Chen, wife of Sun Shen of Hebei, appended to the two Wei and Sui biographies to complete the chapter on exemplary women.
translations.idiomatic: Here we add Zhao, wife of Sun Daowen of Wu, and Chen, wife of Sun Shen of Hebei, to the Wei and Sui accounts so that the chapter on exemplary women may be complete.

sentences.zh: 魏中書侍郎清河崔覽妻封氏者，勃海人，散騎常侍封愷女也。

translations.literal: Feng, wife of Cui Lan, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat of Wei from Qinghe, was a native of Bohai, daughter of Feng Kai, Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, wife of Cui Lan, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat of Wei from Qinghe, came from Bohai. She was the daughter of Feng Kai, Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有才識，聰辯強記，多所究知。

translations.literal: She had talent and insight, was clever in debate and possessed a strong memory, and had investigated and learned much.
translations.idiomatic: She was gifted and discerning, quick in debate and retentive of memory, and had mastered a wide range of learning.

sentences.zh: 時李敷、公孫文叔雖已貴重，近世故事有所不達者，皆就而諮請焉。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fu and Gongsun Wenshu, though already eminent, whenever recent precedents were not clear would all go to consult and inquire of her.
translations.idiomatic: Even Li Fu and Gongsun Wenshu, eminent as they were, would come to her whenever they were uncertain about recent precedents.

sentences.zh: 勃海封卓妻劉氏者，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Feng Zhuo of Bohai, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Feng Zhuo of Bohai, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 成婚一夕，卓官於京師，後以事伏法。

translations.literal: One night after their marriage, Zhuo was serving in the capital; later he was executed by law on account of a case.
translations.idiomatic: They had been married only one night when Zhuo took office in the capital; later he was executed for his involvement in a case.

sentences.zh: 劉氏在家，忽然夢想，知卓已死，哀泣，嫂喻之不止。

translations.literal: Liu at home suddenly dreamed and knew Zhuo was dead; she wept in grief, and her sister-in-law admonished her without stopping her.
translations.idiomatic: At home Liu was suddenly visited in a dream and knew Zhuo was dead. She wept in grief, and though her sister-in-law tried to comfort her, she would not be consoled.

sentences.zh: 經旬，凶問果至，遂憤歎而死。

translations.literal: After ten days the news of death indeed arrived, and she died in grief and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the report of his death arrived, and she died of grief and despair.

sentences.zh: 時人比之秦嘉妻。

translations.literal: People of the time compared her to the wife of Qin Jia.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared her to the wife of Qin Jia.

sentences.zh: 中書令高允念其義高而名不著，為之詩曰：

translations.literal: Chief Minister Gao Yun, mindful that her righteousness was lofty yet her name not renowned, composed a poem for her, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Gao Yun, reflecting that her righteousness was lofty yet her name little known, composed a poem for her:

sentences.zh: 兩儀正位，人倫肇甄。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth took their proper places; human relations were first distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth took their stations; human relations were first ordained.

sentences.zh: 爰制夫婦，統業承先。

translations.literal: Then husband and wife were instituted to carry on the line and inherit the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Then husband and wife were ordained to carry on the line and honor those who came before.

sentences.zh: 雖曰異族，氣猶自然。

translations.literal: Though called different in kind, their spirits are still naturally joined.
translations.idiomatic: Though called different in kind, their spirits are bound as one by nature.

sentences.zh: 生則同室，終契黃泉。

translations.literal: In life they share one chamber; in the end they pledge themselves in the Yellow Springs.
translations.idiomatic: In life they share one room; in death they are pledged in the Yellow Springs below.

sentences.zh: 其一

translations.literal: The first
translations.idiomatic: I

sentences.zh: 封生令達，卓為時彥，內協黃中，外兼三變。

translations.literal: Master Feng was bright and accomplished; Zhuo was a worthy of the age, inwardly harmonious in the golden center, outwardly mastering the three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Master Feng was bright and accomplished; Zhuo was a leading man of the age, inwardly centered in virtue, outwardly versed in the three classic changes.

sentences.zh: 誰能作配，克應其選，實有華宗，挺生淑媛。

translations.literal: Who could be his match? One who could meet that choice—truly there was a noble clan that produced this virtuous lady.
translations.idiomatic: Who could be his match? One worthy of him was found: a noble house had produced this virtuous lady.

sentences.zh: 其二

translations.literal: The second
translations.idiomatic: II

sentences.zh: 京野勢殊，山川乖互，乃奉王命，載馳在路。

translations.literal: Capital and countryside differed in circumstance; mountains and rivers lay far apart; he then received the king's command and hurried on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and countryside lay far apart; mountains and rivers divided them. He received the king's command and hurried on his way.

sentences.zh: 公務既弘，私義獲著，因媒致幣，遘止一幕。

translations.literal: Public duty being weighty, private obligation was fulfilled; through a go-between betrothal gifts were sent, and they met under one roof.
translations.idiomatic: His public duty was heavy, yet private obligation was honored: through a matchmaker betrothal gifts were sent, and they shared one roof as husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 其三

translations.literal: The third
translations.idiomatic: III

sentences.zh: 率我初冠，眷彼弱笄，形由禮比，情以趣諧。

translations.literal: He in his first cap, she with her maiden hairpin—form matched by ritual, feeling joined by inclination.
translations.idiomatic: He had just come of age; she was still a young maiden. Form was joined by ritual, and hearts were drawn together by affection.

sentences.zh: 忻願難常，影跡易乖，悠悠言邁，戚戚長懷。

translations.literal: Joyful wishes are hard to keep constant; shadow and footprint easily part; far the words travel, long the sorrow dwells in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Joy is hard to hold; shadow and footprint soon part. Far he travels on his errand, and long sorrow fills her heart.

sentences.zh: 其四

translations.literal: The fourth
translations.idiomatic: IV

sentences.zh: 時遇險迍，橫罹塵綱，伏質就刑，身分土壤。

translations.literal: The times met with peril; he suddenly fell into the dust of the net; he submitted his body to execution, and body and self returned to soil.
translations.idiomatic: The times turned cruel; he was caught in the dust of the law. He offered his body to execution, and flesh and self returned to earth.

sentences.zh: 千里雖遐，應如影響，良嬪洞感，發於夢想。

translations.literal: Though a thousand li were distant, response came like shadow to sound; the good consort felt it deeply, and it arose in a dream.
translations.idiomatic: Though a thousand li lay between them, her response came like an echo to a sound. The good wife felt it in her depths, and it came to her in a dream.

sentences.zh: 其五

translations.literal: The fifth
translations.idiomatic: V

sentences.zh: 仰惟親命，俯尋嘉好，誰謂會淺，義深情到。

translations.literal: Looking up to parental command, looking down to seek their fine affection—who would say the meeting was shallow? Righteousness was deep, feeling reached its end.
translations.idiomatic: She honored her parents' charge and held fast to their pledged affection. Who would call their meeting brief? Her righteousness ran deep, and her devotion knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 畢志守窮，誓不二醮，何以驗之？

translations.literal: She fulfilled her resolve and kept to poverty, vowing never to marry again—how was this verified?
translations.idiomatic: She fulfilled her resolve and clung to widowhood, vowing never to take another husband. How was this proved?

sentences.zh: 殞身是效。

translations.literal: She gave her life in proof.
translations.idiomatic: She gave her life as proof.

sentences.zh: 其六

translations.literal: The sixth
translations.idiomatic: VI

sentences.zh: 人之處世，孰不厚生？

translations.literal: Among people in the world, who does not cherish life?
translations.idiomatic: Who among the living does not cherish life?

sentences.zh: 必存於義，所重則輕。

translations.literal: She had to preserve righteousness; what was valued became light.
translations.idiomatic: She held to righteousness, and what others valued she held light.

sentences.zh: 結憤鐘心，甘就幽冥，永捐堂宇，長辭母兄。

translations.literal: Grief knotted in her heart, she willingly went to the dark realm, forever leaving the hall and dwelling, long parting from mother and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Grief knotted in her heart, she willingly entered the dark realm, forever leaving her home and taking final leave of mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 其七

translations.literal: The seventh
translations.idiomatic: VII

sentences.zh: 芒芒中野，翳翳孤丘，葛蕾冥蒙，荊棘四周，理苟不昧，神必俱遊。

translations.literal: Vast the central wilds, dim the lonely mound; vines and brambles darkly shroud it, thorns surround on every side—if principle is not obscured, spirits must wander together.
translations.idiomatic: Vast lies the open wild; dim rises the lonely mound. Vines and brambles shroud it, thorns ring it round—yet if truth is not obscured, their spirits must wander together still.

sentences.zh: 異哉貞婦，曠世靡儔。

translations.literal: How extraordinary this chaste wife—through the ages without peer!
translations.idiomatic: How extraordinary this chaste wife—through the ages without equal!

sentences.zh: 其八

translations.literal: The eighth
translations.idiomatic: VIII

sentences.zh: 钜鹿魏溥妻房氏者，慕容垂貴鄉太守常山房湛女也。

translations.literal: Fang, wife of Wei Pu of Julu, was daughter of Fang Zhan, Governor of Guixiang under Murong Chui, from Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, wife of Wei Pu of Julu, was the daughter of Fang Zhan, Governor of Guixiang under Murong Chui, from Changshan.

sentences.zh: 幼有烈操。

translations.literal: From youth she had a fierce integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she possessed a resolute integrity.

sentences.zh: 年十六而溥遇疾，且卒，顧謂之曰：「死不足恨，但痛母老家貧，赤子蒙眇，抱怨於黃壚耳！」

translations.literal: At age sixteen Pu fell ill and was about to die; turning to her he said: 'Death is no great regret, but I grieve that my mother is old and the household poor, and the infant child is blind—resentment in the yellow mound alone!'
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Pu fell gravely ill and, near death, turned to her and said, 'Death itself is no great regret, but it pains me that my mother is old, our household poor, and our infant blind—my only grievance is what I leave behind in the grave!'

sentences.zh: 房垂泣而對曰：「幸承先人餘訓，出事君子，義在偕老，有志不從，蓋其命也。

translations.literal: Fang wept and replied: 'Fortunately I received the leftover teachings of our forebears and went forth to serve a gentleman; righteousness lies in growing old together—if the will is not followed, perhaps it is fate.
translations.idiomatic: Fang wept and answered, 'I have been fortunate to receive my ancestors' teaching and to serve a gentleman. Righteousness demands that we grow old together; if that will cannot be fulfilled, it must be fate.

sentences.zh: 今夫人在堂，弱子衤強褓，顧當以身少相感，永深長往之恨。」

translations.literal: Now my mother-in-law is in the hall and the weak child is in swaddling clothes; I should use my person a little to move them and forever deepen the regret of his long departure.'
translations.idiomatic: Your mother is still alive, and our child is still in swaddling clothes. I must live on a little longer for their sake, though the grief of your going will never leave me.'

sentences.zh: 俄而溥卒。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Pu died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Pu died.

sentences.zh: 及將大斂，房氏操刀割左耳，投之棺中，仍曰：「鬼神有知，相期泉壤。」

translations.literal: When the great encoffining was about to take place, Fang took a knife, cut off her left ear, and cast it into the coffin, saying: 'If spirits have knowledge, let us meet in the springs below.'
translations.idiomatic: When the time came for the encoffining, Fang took a knife, cut off her left ear, and cast it into the coffin, saying, 'If the spirits have knowledge, let us meet in the realm below.'

sentences.zh: 流血滂然，助喪者哀懼。

translations.literal: Blood poured forth; those assisting at the mourning were grieved and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Blood poured forth, and those assisting at the funeral were stricken with grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 姑劉氏輟哭謂曰：「新婦何至於此？」

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law Liu stopped weeping and said: 'New bride, why go to this extent?'
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Liu stopped weeping and said, 'Daughter-in-law, why go so far?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「新婦少年，不幸早寡，實慮父母未量至情，覬持此自誓耳。」

translations.literal: She replied: 'The new bride is young and, unhappily, early widowed; I truly feared my parents would not measure my utmost feeling—I hoped to hold this as a self-pledge.'
translations.idiomatic: She answered, 'I am young and have been widowed too soon. I feared my own parents would not grasp the depth of my devotion, and I wished to pledge myself in this way.'

sentences.zh: 聞知者莫不感愴。

translations.literal: All who heard were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 於時，子緝生未十旬，鞠育於後房之內，未嘗出門。

translations.literal: At that time her son Ji was not yet ten days old; she nursed and reared him within the inner quarters and never went out the door.
translations.idiomatic: At that time her son Ji was not yet ten days old. She nursed and raised him within the inner quarters and never went outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 遂終身不聽絲竹，不預座席。

translations.literal: Thereafter for life she did not listen to string and bamboo music, nor take part in seated feasts.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of her life she would not listen to music or take part in banquets.

sentences.zh: 緝年十二，房父母仍存，於是歸甯，父兄尚有異議。

translations.literal: When Ji was twelve, Fang's parents were still alive; she then went home for a visit, and father and brothers still had objections.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was twelve, Fang's parents were still alive, and she went home for a visit. Her father and brothers still had reservations about her widowhood.

sentences.zh: 緝竊聞之，以啟其母。

translations.literal: Ji secretly heard this and told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ji overheard this and told his mother.

sentences.zh: 房命駕，紿雲他行，因而遂歸。

translations.literal: Fang ordered the carriage, falsely saying she was going elsewhere, and thus returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Fang ordered the carriage, claiming she was going elsewhere, and returned to her husband's home.

sentences.zh: 其家弗之知也。

translations.literal: Her family did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Her own family did not know she had left.

sentences.zh: 行數十里，方覺，兄弟來追，房哀歎而不反。

translations.literal: After traveling several tens of li they realized; her brothers came in pursuit, but Fang lamented and would not return.
translations.idiomatic: After they had gone several tens of li her family realized what had happened. Her brothers came in pursuit, but Fang wept and would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 其執意如此。

translations.literal: Such was the firmness of her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the firmness of her resolve.

sentences.zh: 訓導一子，有母儀法度。

translations.literal: She instructed and guided one son, possessing a mother's model and standards.
translations.idiomatic: She raised and instructed her son with the dignity and discipline of a true mother.

sentences.zh: 緝所交遊，有名勝者，則身具酒饌；

translations.literal: Among Ji's companions, if there were eminent men, she personally prepared wine and food;
translations.idiomatic: When Ji's companions were men of distinction, she personally prepared wine and food for them;

sentences.zh: 有不及己者，輒屏臥不飧，須其悔謝，乃食。

translations.literal: if any were beneath him, she would withdraw to bed and not eat until he repented and apologized, and only then would she eat.
translations.idiomatic: if any were beneath his station, she would withdraw to bed and refuse to eat until he repented and apologized—only then would she take food again.

sentences.zh: 善誘嚴訓，類皆如是。

translations.literal: Skilled in gentle persuasion and strict instruction—such cases were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: In gentle persuasion and strict instruction she was always thus.

sentences.zh: 年六十五而終。

translations.literal: At age sixty-five she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 緝子悅後為濟陰太守，吏民立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Ji's son Yue later became Governor of Jiyin; officials and people erected a stele praising her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Yue later became Governor of Jiyin, and officials and common people erected a stele in praise of her virtue.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫高閭為其文曰：「爰及處士，遘疾夙凋，伉儷秉志，識茂行高，殘形顯操，誓敦久要。」

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Imperial Household Gao Lu wrote its inscription: 'Reaching to the retired gentleman, early stricken and withered; husband and wife held one resolve, knowledge abundant and conduct lofty; mutilating the body to display integrity, vowing the enduring bond.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Imperial Household Gao Lu composed its inscription: 'Reaching to the retired gentleman, early stricken and cut down; husband and wife held one resolve, wisdom rich and conduct lofty; she maimed her body to display her integrity and pledged an enduring bond.'

sentences.zh: 溥未仕而卒，故云處士焉。

translations.literal: Pu died without taking office, hence he is called a retired gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Pu died without ever taking office, hence he is called a retired gentleman.

sentences.zh: 樂部郎胡長命妻張氏者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Hu Changming, Gentleman of the Music Bureau, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Hu Changming of the Music Bureau, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 事姑王氏甚謹。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law Lady Wang with great care.
translations.idiomatic: She served her mother-in-law Lady Wang with great devotion.

sentences.zh: 太安中，京師禁酒。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era wine was forbidden in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era wine was forbidden in the capital.

sentences.zh: 張以姑老且患，私為醖之，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: Zhang, because her mother-in-law was old and ill, privately brewed wine for her and was reported by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Because her mother-in-law was old and ill, Zhang secretly brewed wine for her and was reported by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 王氏詣曹自首，由己私釀。

translations.literal: Lady Wang went to the office and confessed that she herself had brewed privately.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang went to the authorities and confessed that she herself had brewed the wine in secret.

sentences.zh: 張氏曰：「姑老抱患，張主家事，姑不知釀。」

translations.literal: Zhang said: 'My mother-in-law is old and afflicted with illness; Zhang manages the household affairs—the mother-in-law did not know of the brewing.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, 'My mother-in-law is old and ill. I manage the household affairs, and she knew nothing of the brewing.'

sentences.zh: 主司不知所處。

translations.literal: The presiding official did not know how to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: The presiding official did not know how to decide the case.

sentences.zh: 平原王陸麗以狀奏，文成義而赦之。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li memorialized the facts; Emperor Wencheng, moved by righteousness, pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li reported the matter to the throne, and Emperor Wencheng, moved by their righteousness, pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 平原鄃縣女子孫氏男玉者，夫為零陵縣人所殺。

translations.literal: Nanyu, daughter of the Sun family of Shuxian in Pingyuan, had a husband killed by a man of Lingling County.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyu, daughter of the Sun family of Shuxian in Pingyuan, had a husband who was murdered by a man from Lingling County.

sentences.zh: 男玉追執仇人，欲自殺之。

translations.literal: Nanyu pursued and seized the enemy, wishing to kill him herself.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyu pursued and seized the murderer, intending to kill him herself.

sentences.zh: 其弟止而不聽。

translations.literal: Her younger brother stopped her but she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother tried to stop her, but she would not listen.

sentences.zh: 男玉曰：「女人出適，以夫為天，當親自復雪，云何假人之手？」

translations.literal: Nanyu said: 'When a woman marries out, she takes her husband as Heaven; she ought personally to exact vengeance—how can she borrow another's hand?'
translations.idiomatic: Nanyu said, 'When a woman marries, her husband is her heaven. I must avenge him myself—how could I leave it to another's hand?'

sentences.zh: 遂以杖毆殺之。

translations.literal: She then beat him to death with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: She then beat him to death with a staff.

sentences.zh: 有司處死，以聞。

translations.literal: The authorities sentenced her to death and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities sentenced her to death and reported the case to the throne.

sentences.zh: 獻文詔曰：「男玉重節輕身，以義犯法，緣情定罪，理在可原，其特恕之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen decreed: 'Nanyu valued integrity and held life lightly; she violated the law for righteousness. Considering feeling in fixing punishment, principle allows pardon—let her be specially forgiven.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen decreed, 'Nanyu valued integrity above her own life and broke the law for righteousness' sake. When feeling is weighed in judgment, she may be pardoned. Let her be specially forgiven.'

sentences.zh: 清河房愛親妻崔氏者，同郡崔元孫之女也。

translations.literal: Cui, wife of Fang Aiqin of Qinghe, was daughter of Cui Yuansun of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, wife of Fang Aiqin of Qinghe, was the daughter of Cui Yuansun of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 性嚴明，有高節，歷覽書傳，多所聞知。

translations.literal: Her nature was stern and clear; she had lofty integrity, had read through books and records, and knew much.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern and principled, possessed of lofty integrity, and had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 親授子景伯、景光《九經》義，學行修明，並當世名士。

translations.literal: She personally taught her sons Jingbo and Jingguang the meaning of the Nine Classics; their learning and conduct were cultivated and bright, and both were eminent men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: She personally taught her sons Jingbo and Jingguang the meaning of the Nine Classics. Both became men of cultivated learning and conduct, eminent in their generation.

sentences.zh: 景伯為清河太守，每有疑獄，常先請焉。

translations.literal: Jingbo was Governor of Qinghe; whenever there was a doubtful case, he would first consult her.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo served as Governor of Qinghe, and whenever a case was doubtful he would consult her first.

sentences.zh: 貝丘人列子不孝，吏欲案之，景伯為之悲傷，入白其母。

translations.literal: A man of Beiqiu named Liezi was unfilial; the clerks wished to prosecute him. Jingbo was grieved for him and went in to tell his mother.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Beiqiu named Liezi was unfilial, and the clerks wished to prosecute him. Jingbo was moved to pity and went to tell his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「吾聞聞名不如見面，小人未見禮教，何足責哉！

translations.literal: His mother said: 'I have heard that to hear a name is not as good as to see the face; petty men who have not seen ritual teaching—how can they be blamed!
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, 'They say that hearing of someone is not like meeting him face to face. A petty man who has never been taught ritual propriety—how can he be blamed?

sentences.zh: 但呼其母來，吾與之同居，其子置汝左右，令其見汝事吾，或應自改。」

translations.literal: Only summon his mother here; I will dwell with her together. Place his son at your side and let him see how you serve me—perhaps he will reform himself.'
translations.idiomatic: Summon his mother here and let me live with her. Place his son at your side and let him watch how you serve me—perhaps he will reform himself.'

sentences.zh: 景伯遂召其母，崔氏處之於榻，與之共食。

translations.literal: Jingbo then summoned the mother; Cui placed her on the couch and ate with her together.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo summoned the mother, and Cui received her on a couch and shared meals with her.

sentences.zh: 景伯為之溫凊。

translations.literal: Jingbo attended to her warmth and coolness for her.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo himself saw to her comfort in heat and cold.

sentences.zh: 其子侍立堂下，未及旬日，悔過求還。

translations.literal: His son stood waiting in the hall below; before ten days had passed, he repented and asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The son stood waiting in the hall below. Before ten days had passed, he repented and asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 崔氏曰：「此雖顏慚，未知心愧，且可置之。」

translations.literal: Cui said: 'Though his face shows shame, we do not yet know whether his heart feels remorse—for now let it be set aside.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui said, 'His face may show shame, but we do not yet know whether his heart feels remorse. For now let it be set aside.'

sentences.zh: 凡經二十餘日，其子叩頭流血，其母涕泣乞還，然後聽之，終以孝聞。

translations.literal: In all more than twenty days passed; the son knocked his head until it bled, and his mother wept and begged to return home—only then did she permit it. In the end he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days the son knocked his head until it bled, and his mother wept and begged to return home. Only then did she allow it. In the end he became renowned for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 其識度勵物如此。

translations.literal: Such was her insight and her power to encourage others.
translations.idiomatic: Such was her insight and her power to move others to reform.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: In the end she died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: She lived out her full span of years.

sentences.zh: 涇州貞女兒氏者，許嫁彭老生為妻。

translations.literal: Er, the chaste woman of Jingzhou, was betrothed to marry Peng Laosheng as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Er, the chaste woman of Jingzhou, had been betrothed to Peng Laosheng.

sentences.zh: 聘幣既畢，未及成禮。

translations.literal: The betrothal gifts were complete, but the wedding ceremony had not yet taken place.
translations.idiomatic: The betrothal gifts had been exchanged, but the wedding had not yet been held.

sentences.zh: 兒氏率行貞淑，居貧，常自舂汲，以養父母。

translations.literal: Er's conduct was chaste and virtuous; living in poverty, she often pounded grain and drew water herself to support her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Er was chaste and virtuous in her conduct. Though poor, she often pounded grain and drew water herself to support her parents.

sentences.zh: 老生輒往逼之，女曰：「與君聘命雖畢，二門多故，未及相見，何由不稟父母，擅見陵辱！

translations.literal: Laosheng repeatedly went to force her. The girl said: 'Though our betrothal is complete, both families have many affairs and we have not yet met—how can you fail to inform our parents and on your own come to insult and violate me!
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng repeatedly came to force her. The girl said, 'Though our betrothal is complete, both our families have many affairs and we have not yet even met. How can you fail to inform our parents and come on your own to insult and violate me?

sentences.zh: 若苟行非禮，正可身死耳！」

translations.literal: If you rashly act against ritual, I can only die in body!'
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on violating propriety, I can only die!'

sentences.zh: 遂不肯從。

translations.literal: She then refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: She refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 老生怒而刺殺之，取其衣服。

translations.literal: Laosheng in anger stabbed and killed her and took her clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng in anger stabbed her to death and took her clothes.

sentences.zh: 女尚能言，臨死謂老生曰：「生身何罪，與君相遇！

translations.literal: The girl could still speak; on the point of death she said to Laosheng: 'What crime did this life commit to meet you!
translations.idiomatic: The girl could still speak. On the point of death she said to Laosheng, 'What crime did I commit in this life to meet you!

sentences.zh: 我所以執節自固者，寧更有所邀，正欲奉給君耳。

translations.literal: The reason I held to my integrity and stood firm was not that I had some other invitation—I only wished to serve and give myself to you.
translations.idiomatic: I held to my integrity not because I sought anything else, but because I wished to give myself to you alone.

sentences.zh: 今反為君所殺，若魂靈有知，自當相報。」

translations.literal: Now instead I am killed by you; if spirits have knowledge, they will surely repay this.'
translations.idiomatic: Now you have killed me instead. If spirits have knowledge, they will surely repay you.'

sentences.zh: 言終而絕。

translations.literal: When her words ended, she died.
translations.idiomatic: With these words she died.

sentences.zh: 老生持女衣服珠纓，至其叔宅，以告。

translations.literal: Laosheng took the girl's clothes and pearl tassels to her uncle's house and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng took the girl's clothes and pearl ornaments to her uncle's house and told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 叔曰：「此是汝婦，奈何殺之，天不祐汝！」

translations.literal: The uncle said: 'This was your wife—how could you kill her? Heaven will not protect you!'
translations.idiomatic: The uncle said, 'This was your betrothed wife—how could you kill her? Heaven will not protect you!'

sentences.zh: 遂執送官。

translations.literal: He then seized him and sent him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: He seized him and handed him over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，有司劾以死罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe the authorities impeached him for the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe the authorities impeached him for a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「老生不仁，侵陵貞淑，原其強暴，便可戮之，而女守禮履節，沒身不改，雖處草莽，行合古跡。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Laosheng was without benevolence and violated the chaste and virtuous; considering his violence, he may be executed. The girl kept ritual and practiced integrity, unchanged to the end; though she dwelt in the wilds, her conduct matched ancient traces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, 'Laosheng was cruel and violated a chaste and virtuous woman. Considering his violence, he may be executed. The girl kept ritual and practiced integrity to the end of her life. Though she lived in humble circumstances, her conduct matched the deeds of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宜賜美名，以顯風操，其標墓旌善，號曰『貞女』」。

translations.literal: She should be granted a fine name to display her moral conduct; mark her tomb and praise her goodness, and give her the title "Chaste Woman."'
translations.idiomatic: Grant her a fine name to display her moral conduct. Mark her tomb and praise her virtue, and give her the title Chaste Woman.'

sentences.zh: 姚氏婦楊氏者，閹人苻承祖姨也。

translations.literal: Yang, wife of the Yao family, was aunt to the eunuch Fu Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, wife of the Yao family, was the aunt of the eunuch Fu Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 家貧。

translations.literal: Her family was poor.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was poor.

sentences.zh: 及承祖為文明太后所寵貴，親姻皆求利潤，唯楊獨不欲。

translations.literal: When Chengzu was favored and ennobled by Empress Dowager Wenming, kin by marriage all sought profit—only Yang alone did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu was favored and ennobled by Empress Dowager Wenming, all his kin by marriage sought profit from his rise—only Yang wanted none of it.

sentences.zh: 常謂其姊曰：「姊雖有一時之榮，不若妹有無憂之樂。」

translations.literal: She often said to her elder sister: 'Though you have glory for a time, it is not like my sister having the joy of freedom from worry.'
translations.idiomatic: She often said to her elder sister, 'Sister, you may have glory for a time, but that is not like the joy I have in living without worry.'

sentences.zh: 姊每遺其衣服，多不受。

translations.literal: Whenever her sister sent her clothing, she mostly would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever her sister sent her clothing, she mostly refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 強與之，則云：「我夫家世貧，好衣美服則使人不安。」

translations.literal: If forced to take them, she would say: 'My husband's family has been poor for generations; fine clothes and beautiful garments would make people uneasy.'
translations.idiomatic: If they forced them on her, she would say, 'My husband's family has been poor for generations. Fine clothes would make people uneasy.'

sentences.zh: 與之奴婢，云：「我家無食，不能供給。」

translations.literal: When given maidservants, she said: 'My household has no food and cannot support them.'
translations.idiomatic: When given maidservants, she said, 'My household has no food and cannot support them.'

sentences.zh: 終不肯受。

translations.literal: In the end she would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 常著破衣，自執勞事。

translations.literal: She constantly wore tattered clothes and performed labor herself.
translations.idiomatic: She always wore tattered clothes and performed labor with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 時受其衣服，多不著，密埋之。

translations.literal: When she did accept clothing, she mostly did not wear it and secretly buried it.
translations.idiomatic: When she did accept clothing, she mostly did not wear it and secretly buried it away.

sentences.zh: 設有著者，汙之而後服。

translations.literal: If she did wear any, she would soil it first and only then put it on.
translations.idiomatic: If she did wear any, she would soil it first before putting it on.

sentences.zh: 承祖每見其寒悴，深恨其家，謂不供給之。

translations.literal: Whenever Chengzu saw her cold and wasted, he deeply resented her family, saying they did not provide for her.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chengzu saw her cold and emaciated, he deeply resented her family, believing they did not provide for her.

sentences.zh: 乃啟其母曰：「今承祖一身，何所乏少，而使姨如是？」

translations.literal: He then told his mother: 'Now Chengzu alone—what does he lack? Yet my aunt is like this!'
translations.idiomatic: He told his mother, 'Now that Chengzu alone lacks for nothing, why is my aunt in such a state?'

sentences.zh: 母具以語之。

translations.literal: His mother told him the full story.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told him the full story.

sentences.zh: 承祖乃遣人乘車往迎之，則厲志不起。

translations.literal: Chengzu then sent men in a carriage to welcome her, but with stern resolve she would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu then sent men in a carriage to fetch her, but with stern resolve she would not go.

sentences.zh: 遣人強輦於車上，則大哭言：「爾欲殺我也！」

translations.literal: When men were sent to force her onto the carriage, she wept loudly and said: 'You wish to kill me!'
translations.idiomatic: When men were sent to force her into the carriage, she wept loudly and cried, 'You wish to kill me!'

sentences.zh: 由是苻家內外，皆號為癡姨。

translations.literal: From this, inside and outside the Fu household all called her the mad aunt.
translations.idiomatic: From this, everyone inside and outside the Fu household called her the mad aunt.

sentences.zh: 及承祖敗，有司執其二姨至殿庭致法，以姚氏婦衣裳弊陋，特免其罪。

translations.literal: When Chengzu fell, the authorities seized his two aunts to the palace court to apply the law; because the Yao family's wife's clothes were worn and shabby, her crime was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu fell, the authorities seized his two aunts to the palace court for punishment. Because the Yao family's wife wore worn and shabby clothes, her crime was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其識機，雖呂嬃亦不如也。

translations.literal: Her discernment of the times—even Lü Wei was not her equal.
translations.idiomatic: Her discernment of the times—even Lü Wei could not match her.

sentences.zh: 滎陽京縣人張洪祁妻劉氏者，年十七夫亡。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Zhang Hongqi of Jing County in Xingyang, was seventeen when her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Zhang Hongqi of Jing County in Xingyang, was seventeen when her husband died.

sentences.zh: 遺腹生一子，三歲又沒。

translations.literal: She bore a posthumous son; at three years he also died.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a posthumous son, who died at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 其舅姑年老，朝夕奉養，率禮無違。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law were old; morning and evening she served and supported them, observing ritual without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law were elderly. Morning and evening she served them, observing ritual without fail.

sentences.zh: 兄矜其少寡，欲奪嫁之，劉自誓不許，以終其身。

translations.literal: Her elder brother pitied her young widowhood and wished to force her to remarry; Liu vowed and would not consent, remaining so for life.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother pitied her young widowhood and wished to force her to remarry. Liu vowed she would not consent and remained a widow for life.

sentences.zh: 陳留董景起妻張氏者，景起早亡，張時年十六，，痛夫少喪，哀傷過禮，蔬食長齋。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Dong Jingqi of Chenliu—Jingqi died early; Zhang was then sixteen, grieved that her husband died young, mourned beyond ritual, ate vegetables and kept long fasts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Dong Jingqi of Chenliu: Jingqi died early when Zhang was sixteen. Grieving that her husband had died so young, she mourned beyond what ritual required, ate only vegetables, and kept long fasts.

sentences.zh: 又無兒息，獨守貞操，期以闔棺。

translations.literal: She had no sons or heirs and alone kept chaste integrity, expecting to share the coffin at the close.
translations.idiomatic: She had no children and alone kept her chaste integrity, resolved to share his coffin at the end.

sentences.zh: 鄉曲高之，終見標異。

translations.literal: Neighbors and locals honored her; in the end she was marked out as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors honored her, and in the end she was publicly recognized for her virtue.

sentences.zh: 漁陽太守陽尼妻高氏者，勃海人也。

translations.literal: Gao, wife of Yang Ni, Governor of Yuyang, was a native of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, wife of Yang Ni, Governor of Yuyang, was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 學識有文翰，孝文敕令入侍後宮。

translations.literal: She had learning and knowledge and possessed literary composition; Emperor Xiaowen ordered her to enter and serve in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was learned and skilled in literary composition. Emperor Xiaowen ordered her to enter and serve in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 幽後表啟，悉其辭也。

translations.literal: The memorials and reports of Empress You were all in her wording.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials and reports of Empress You were all composed in her words.

sentences.zh: 滎陽史映周妻耿氏者，同郡耿氏女也。

translations.literal: Geng, wife of Shi Yingzhou of Xingyang, was daughter of the Geng family of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Geng, wife of Shi Yingzhou of Xingyang, was the daughter of the Geng family of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十七，適於映周。

translations.literal: At seventeen she married Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen she married Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太和二十三年，映周卒，耿氏恐父母奪其志，因葬映周，哀哭而殞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe Yingzhou died. Geng feared her parents would wrest away her resolve; at Yingzhou's burial she wailed in grief and perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Taihe Yingzhou died. Geng feared her parents would force her to remarry. At his burial she wailed in grief and died.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不悲歎。

translations.literal: All who saw it were grieved and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 屬大使觀風，以狀具上，詔標門閭。

translations.literal: When an envoy came to observe local customs, the facts were fully reported upward, and an edict marked her gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came to observe local customs, the matter was fully reported to the throne, and an edict marked her gate and lane with honor.

sentences.zh: 任城國太妃孟氏者，钜鹿人，尚書、任城王澄之母也。

translations.literal: Meng, Grand Consort of the State of Rencheng, was a native of Julu, mother of the Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, Grand Consort of the State of Rencheng, was from Julu and was the mother of Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄為揚州之日，率眾出討。

translations.literal: When Cheng was in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng was serving in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.

sentences.zh: 於後賊帥姜慶真陰結逆黨，襲陷羅城。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandit chief Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined rebellious factions and in a surprise attack seized Luocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the rebel leader Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined with traitors and in a surprise attack seized Luocheng.

sentences.zh: 長史韋纘倉卒，孟乃勒兵登陴，激厲文武，喻之逆順。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wei Zuan was caught off guard; Meng then marshaled troops, mounted the battlements, roused civil and military officials, and explained to them loyalty and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wei Zuan was caught off guard. Meng then marshaled the troops, mounted the battlements, roused the civil and military officials, and explained to them the difference between loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 於是咸有奮志，賊不能克，卒以全城。

translations.literal: Thereupon all had fighting spirit; the rebels could not overcome them, and in the end the whole city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all took heart for the fight. The rebels could not overcome them, and in the end the whole city was preserved.

sentences.zh: 靈太后後敕有司樹碑旌美。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered the authorities to erect a stele praising her excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered the authorities to erect a stele in praise of her excellence.

sentences.zh: 梓潼太守苟金龍妻劉氏者，平原人也，廷尉少卿劉叔宗之姊也。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Gou Jinlong, Governor of Zitong, was a native of Pingyuan, elder sister of Liu Shuzong, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Gou Jinlong, Governor of Zitong, was from Pingyuan and was the elder sister of Liu Shuzong, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，金龍為郡，帶關城戍主。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuanwu, Jinlong was governor of the commandery and concurrently commander of the Guancheng garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xuanwu, Jinlong served as governor of the commandery and concurrently as commander of the Guancheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 梁人攻圍，會金龍疾病，不堪部分，劉遂厲城人修理戰具，夜悉登城拒戰，百有餘日，兵士死傷過半。

translations.literal: Liang forces besieged them; Jinlong fell ill and could not command. Liu then urged the people of the city to repair weapons, and at night all mounted the walls to resist; for more than a hundred days soldiers killed and wounded exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: Liang forces besieged the city. Jinlong fell ill and could not command. Liu then urged the townspeople to repair weapons, and at night all mounted the walls to resist. For more than a hundred days the fighting continued, and more than half the soldiers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 戍副高景陰圖叛逆，劉與城人斬景及其黨與數十人。

translations.literal: Deputy garrison commander Gao Jing secretly plotted rebellion; Liu with the people of the city beheaded Jing and several tens of his associates.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy garrison commander Gao Jing secretly plotted rebellion. Liu and the townspeople beheaded Jing and several dozen of his associates.

sentences.zh: 自餘將士，分衣減食，勞逸必同，莫不畏而懷之。

translations.literal: The remaining officers and soldiers shared clothing and reduced food; in toil and rest they were always alike—none did not fear and cherish her.
translations.idiomatic: She shared clothing and reduced rations with the remaining officers and soldiers, sharing their toil and rest alike. All feared and revered her.

sentences.zh: 井在外城，尋為賊陷，城中絕水，渴死者多。

translations.literal: The wells were in the outer city and soon fell to the enemy; within the city water was cut off and many died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The wells lay in the outer city and soon fell to the enemy. Within the city water was cut off, and many died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 劉乃集諸長幼，喻以忠節，遂相率告訴於天，俱時號叫，俄而澍雨。

translations.literal: Liu then gathered elders and young, explained loyalty and integrity to them, and together they appealed to Heaven, all crying out at once; shortly a soaking rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liu then gathered young and old, explained loyalty and integrity to them, and together they appealed to Heaven, all crying out at once. Shortly afterward a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 劉命出公私布絹及至衣服，懸之城內，絞而取水，所有雜器，悉儲之。

translations.literal: Liu ordered public and private cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, wrung to draw water, and all vessels stored.
translations.idiomatic: Liu ordered public and private cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, and wrung to draw water. Every vessel was put to use.

sentences.zh: 於是人心益固。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people's hearts grew firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people's resolve grew firmer still.

sentences.zh: 會益州刺史傅豎眼將至，梁人乃退。

translations.literal: When Governor of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was about to arrive, the Liang forces then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was about to arrive, the Liang forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 豎眼歎異之，具狀奏聞。

translations.literal: Shuyan sighed in wonder and fully reported the facts to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan marveled at her deeds and fully reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu commended her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu commended her.

sentences.zh: 正光中，賞其子慶珍平昌縣子，又得二子出身。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era her son Qingzhen was rewarded with the title Marquis of Pingchang County, and two more sons received initial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era her son Qingzhen was ennobled as Marquis of Pingchang County, and two more sons received initial appointment to office.

sentences.zh: 貞孝女宗者，趙郡柏人人，趙郡太守李叔胤之女，范陽盧元禮之妻也。

translations.literal: Zong, the chaste and filial daughter, was a native of Bo in Zhao Commandery, daughter of Li Shuyin, Governor of Zhao Commandery, and wife of Lu Yuanli of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, the chaste and filial daughter, was from Bo in Zhao Commandery, the daughter of Li Shuyin, Governor of Zhao Commandery, and the wife of Lu Yuanli of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父卒，號慟幾絕者數四，賴母崔氏慰勉之，得全。

translations.literal: Her nature was utmost in filial piety; when her father died she wailed and nearly expired four times, and only through her mother Lady Cui's comfort and encouragement did she survive.
translations.idiomatic: She was utterly filial by nature. When her father died she wailed until she nearly expired four times, and only through her mother Lady Cui's comfort and encouragement did she survive.

sentences.zh: 三年之中，形骸銷瘠，非人不起。

translations.literal: Within three years her body wasted away; unless someone came she would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years her body wasted away, and she would not rise unless someone came to her.

sentences.zh: 及歸夫氏，與母分隔，便飲食日損，涕泣不絕，日就羸篤。

translations.literal: When she returned to her husband's family and was separated from her mother, her food and drink daily diminished, tears flowed without cease, and day by day she grew frail and grave.
translations.idiomatic: When she returned to her husband's family and was separated from her mother, her food and drink daily diminished, tears flowed without cease, and day by day she grew frail and grave.

sentences.zh: 盧氏闔家慰喻，不解。

translations.literal: The whole Lu household comforted and admonished her, but she would not be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Lu household comforted and admonished her, but she would not be consoled.

sentences.zh: 因遣歸寧還家，乃復故。

translations.literal: They therefore sent her home for a visit, and only then did she recover.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore sent her home for a visit, and only then did she recover.

sentences.zh: 如此者八九焉。

translations.literal: This happened eight or nine times.
translations.idiomatic: This happened eight or nine times.

sentences.zh: 及元禮卒，李追亡撫遺，事姑以孝謹著。

translations.literal: When Yuanli died, Li pursued the departed and nurtured the survivors, serving her mother-in-law with filial care and becoming known for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanli died, Li mourned the departed and nurtured the survivors, serving her mother-in-law with filial devotion and becoming renowned for it.

sentences.zh: 母崔終於洛陽，凶問初到，舉聲慟絕，一宿乃蘇，水漿不入口者六日。

translations.literal: Her mother Cui died in Luoyang; when the news of death first arrived, she raised her voice in grief and fainted, reviving only after one night; for six days she took no water or food.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Cui died in Luoyang. When the news first arrived, she raised her voice in grief and fainted, reviving only after a night had passed. For six days she took no water or food.

sentences.zh: 其姑慮其不濟，親送奔喪，而氣力危殆，自范陽向都，八旬方達。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law feared she would not survive and personally escorted her to rush to the funeral; her strength was perilously weak—from Fanyang toward the capital, eighty days before she arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law feared she would not survive and personally escorted her to the funeral. Her strength was perilously weak—from Fanyang to the capital it took eighty days before she arrived.

sentences.zh: 攀櫬號踴，遂卒。

translations.literal: Clinging to the coffin she wailed and stamped; then she died.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to the coffin she wailed and stamped in grief, and then she died.

sentences.zh: 有司以狀聞，詔追號貞孝女宗，易其裏為孝德里，樹李、盧二門，以惇風俗。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the facts; an edict posthumously gave her the title Chaste and Filial Daughter Zong, changed her lane to Xiaode Lane, and erected markers at the Li and Lu gates to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the facts to the throne. An edict posthumously gave her the title Chaste and Filial Daughter Zong, changed her lane to Lane of Filial Virtue, and erected markers at the Li and Lu gates to encourage moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 河東姚氏女者，字女勝。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Yao family of Hedong had the courtesy name Nüsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the Yao family of Hedong had the courtesy name Nüsheng.

sentences.zh: 少喪父，無兄弟，母憐而守養。

translations.literal: She lost her father young, had no brothers, and her mother pitied and raised her.
translations.idiomatic: She lost her father young, had no brothers, and her mother pitied and raised her alone.

sentences.zh: 年六七歲，便有孝性，人言其父者，聞輒垂泣，鄰伍異之。

translations.literal: At six or seven years she already had filial nature; when people spoke of her father, hearing it she would at once weep—neighbors found it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At six or seven she already showed filial nature. Whenever people spoke of her father, she would weep at once. Her neighbors marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 正光中母死，勝年十五，哭泣不絕聲，水漿不入口者數日，不勝哀，遂死。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era her mother died; Sheng was fifteen, wept without cease, took no water or food for several days, could not bear the grief, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era her mother died. Sheng was fifteen. She wept without cease and took no water or food for several days. Unable to bear her grief, she died.

sentences.zh: 太守崔游申請為營墓立碑，自為制文，表其門閭，比之曹娥，改其裏曰上虞裏。

translations.literal: Governor Cui You petitioned to build her tomb and erect a stele, composed the inscription himself, marked her gate and lane, compared her to Cao E, and changed her lane to Shangyu Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Cui You petitioned to build her tomb and erect a stele, composed the inscription himself, marked her gate and lane with honor, compared her to Cao E, and changed her lane to Shangyu Lane.

sentences.zh: 墓在都城東六里，大道北，至今名為孝女塚。

translations.literal: Her tomb is six li east of the capital, north of the great road; to this day it is called the Tomb of the Filial Daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her tomb lies six li east of the capital, north of the great road. To this day it is called the Tomb of the Filial Daughter.

sentences.zh: 滎陽刁思遵妻者，魯氏女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Diao Sizun of Xingyang was daughter of the Lu family.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Diao Sizun of Xingyang was a daughter of the Lu family.

sentences.zh: 始笄為思遵所聘，未逾月而思遵亡。

translations.literal: At her first hairpin she was betrothed to Sizun; before a month had passed Sizun died.
translations.idiomatic: At her coming of age she was betrothed to Sizun, but before a month had passed he died.

sentences.zh: 其家矜其少寡，許嫁已定。

translations.literal: Her family pitied her young widowhood; a betrothal for remarriage was already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Her family pitied her young widowhood, and a betrothal for remarriage was already settled.

sentences.zh: 魯聞之，以死自誓。

translations.literal: Lu heard of it and vowed on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu heard of it, she vowed she would rather die.

sentences.zh: 父母不達其志，遂經郡訴，稱刁氏吝護寡女，不使歸寧。

translations.literal: Her parents did not understand her intent and so appealed to the commandery, charging the Diao family with stingily guarding the widow and not allowing her to visit home.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents did not understand her intent and appealed to the commandery, charging the Diao family with stingily guarding the widow and not allowing her to visit her own home.

sentences.zh: 魯乃與老姑徒步詣司徒府，自告情狀。

translations.literal: Lu then with her aged mother-in-law went on foot to the Secretariat and reported her situation herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu then went on foot with her aged mother-in-law to the Secretariat and reported her situation herself.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，有司聞奏，節閔詔本司依式標榜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai the authorities heard and memorialized; Emperor Jiemin decreed that the relevant office mark her gate according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai the authorities heard and memorialized. Emperor Jiemin decreed that the relevant office mark her gate with honor according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 西魏武功縣孫道溫妻趙氏者，安平人也。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Sun Daowen of Wugong County in Western Wei, was a native of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of Sun Daowen of Wugong County in Western Wei, was from Anping.

sentences.zh: 万俟醜奴之反，圍岐州，久之無援。

translations.literal: When Moqi Chounu rebelled, he besieged Qizhou; after a long while there was no relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Moqi Chounu rebelled, he besieged Qizhou, and after a long time no relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 趙乃謂城中婦女曰：「今州城方陷，義在同憂。」

translations.literal: Zhao then said to the women in the city: "Now the prefectural city is about to fall; it is right that we share the same worry."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then said to the women in the city, "The prefectural city is on the verge of falling—we ought to share the same anxiety.

sentences.zh: 遂相率負土，晝夜培城，城竟免賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led one another carrying earth, day and night reinforcing the walls, and the city ultimately escaped the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They then led one another in carrying earth, reinforcing the walls day and night, and the city was ultimately spared from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大統六年，贈夫岐州刺史，贈趙安平縣君。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong, her husband was posthumously made Prefect of Qizhou, and Zhao was posthumously made Lady of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Datong, her husband was posthumously appointed Prefect of Qizhou, and Zhao was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Anping County.

sentences.zh: 河北孫神妻陳氏者，河北郡人也。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Sun Shen of Hebei, was a native of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Sun Shen of Hebei, was from Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 神當遠戍，主吏配在夏州，意難其遠。

translations.literal: Shen was to go on distant frontier service; the chief clerk assigned him to Xiazhou, and he balked at the distance.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was to serve on a distant frontier posting; the chief clerk assigned him to Xiazhou, and he found the distance hard to accept.

sentences.zh: 有孤兄子，欲以自代。

translations.literal: He had an orphaned elder brother's son and wished to send him in his own place.
translations.idiomatic: He had an orphaned nephew and wanted to send him in his stead.

sentences.zh: 陳曰：「為國征戍，道路遼遠，何容身不肯行，以孤侄自代！

translations.literal: Chen said: "To go on campaign for the state—the road is vast and far. How could one's own body refuse to go and send an orphaned nephew in one's place!
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "To go on campaign for the state—the road is vast and far. How could you refuse to go yourself and send an orphaned nephew in your place!

sentences.zh: 天下物議，誰其相許？」

translations.literal: Among the talk of the world, who would approve?"
translations.idiomatic: What man under heaven would countenance such a thing in the court of public opinion?

sentences.zh: 神感其言，乃自行。

translations.literal: Shen was moved by her words and went himself.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her words, Shen went himself.

sentences.zh: 在戍未幾，便喪。

translations.literal: At the garrison, before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the garrison he died before long.

sentences.zh: 忄彗柩至，陳望而哀慟，一哭而卒。

translations.literal: When the coffin arrived, Chen looked upon it and wailed in grief; with one cry she died.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin arrived, Chen gazed at it and wailed in grief; with a single cry she died.

sentences.zh: 文帝詔表其閭。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen decreed that her lane be marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen decreed that her neighborhood be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 隋蘭陵公主字阿五，文帝第五女也。

translations.literal: Princess Lanling of Sui, courtesy name A-Wu, was the Emperor's fifth daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling of Sui, whose courtesy name was A-Wu, was Emperor Wen's fifth daughter.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，性婉順，帝於諸女中，特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Beautiful in appearance, mild and obedient in nature—among all his daughters the Emperor especially cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: She was beautiful in appearance and gentle in temperament; among all his daughters the Emperor cherished her above the rest.

sentences.zh: 初嫁儀同王奉孝。

translations.literal: She was first married to Wang Fengxiao, an honorary official of the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to Wang Fengxiao, a gentleman of parallel rank.

sentences.zh: 奉孝卒，適河東柳述，時年十八。

translations.literal: When Fengxiao died, she was given in marriage to Liu Shu of Hedong, at the age of eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: After Fengxiao died, she was remarried to Liu Shu of Hedong at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 諸姊並驕踞，主獨折節遵婦道，事舅姑甚謹，遇疾必親奉湯藥。

translations.literal: All her elder sisters were haughty and overbearing; the princess alone lowered herself and followed the wife's way, serving her parents-in-law with great care, and whenever they fell ill she always personally presented medicine.
translations.idiomatic: All her elder sisters were proud and domineering, but the princess alone humbled herself and observed a wife's duties, serving her parents-in-law with scrupulous care and always personally bringing them medicine when they fell ill.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大悅，由是述漸見寵遇。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of this with great delight, and from this Liu Shu gradually came into favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased to hear of this, and from then on Liu Shu gradually won favor.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王廣欲以主配其妃弟蕭瑒，文帝將許之，後遂適述，晉王因不悅。

translations.literal: Initially, Prince of Jin Yang Guang wished to marry the princess to Xiao Chang, younger brother of his consort; Emperor Wen was about to agree, but afterward she was given to Liu Shu, and the Prince of Jin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince of Jin Yang Guang wanted to marry the princess to Xiao Chang, younger brother of his consort; Emperor Wen was about to consent, but in the end she was given to Liu Shu instead, and the Prince of Jin was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及述用事，彌惡之。

translations.literal: When Liu Shu came into power, he hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shu came into power, the prince hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，述徙嶺表。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Liu Shu was banished beyond the mountains to the south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Liu Shu was exiled to the far south beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 煬帝令主與述離絕，將改嫁之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered the princess to sever ties with Liu Shu and intended to remarry her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered the princess to break with Liu Shu and planned to marry her to someone else.

sentences.zh: 公主以死自誓，不復朝謁，表求免主號，與述同徙。

translations.literal: The princess swore on pain of death, no longer attended court audiences, and submitted a memorial asking to be stripped of her princess title and exiled with Liu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess vowed she would rather die, stopped attending court, and submitted a memorial asking to be stripped of her princess title and exiled together with Liu Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「天下豈無男子，欲與述同徙邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor raged: "Is there no man under heaven that you wish to go into exile with Liu Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and said, "Are there no men under heaven that you wish to go into exile with Liu Shu?

sentences.zh: 主曰：「先帝以妾適柳家，今其有罪，妾當從坐。」

translations.literal: The princess said: "The late Emperor gave me in marriage to the Liu family; now that he has committed a crime, I should suffer punishment along with him."
translations.idiomatic: The princess replied, "The late Emperor gave me in marriage to the Liu family. Now that he has committed a crime, I ought to share his punishment."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 主憂憤卒，時年三十二。

translations.literal: The princess died of grief and indignation, at the age of thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died of grief and indignation at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 臨終上表：生不得從夫死，乞葬柳氏。

translations.literal: On her deathbed she submitted a memorial: having been unable to follow her husband in life, she begged to be buried in the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she submitted a memorial: unable to follow her husband in life, she begged to be buried with the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 帝覽表愈怒，竟不哭，葬主於洪瀆川，資送甚薄。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and grew angrier still; he did not weep at all, and buried the princess at Hongdu River with very meager provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and grew still angrier; he did not weep at all, and buried the princess at Hongdu River with very meager funeral provisions.

sentences.zh: 朝野傷之。

translations.literal: Court and commoners alike mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: All through court and countryside, people mourned her.

sentences.zh: 南陽公主者，煬帝長女也。

translations.literal: Princess Nanyang was Emperor Yang's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Nanyang was the eldest daughter of Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，有志節。

translations.literal: Graceful in bearing, she had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: She was graceful in bearing and possessed firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 十四嫁於許國公宇文述子士及，以謹厚聞。

translations.literal: At fourteen she married Yu Shiji, son of Duke of Xu Yuwen Shu, and was known for her careful steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she married Yu Shiji, son of Duke of Xu Yuwen Shu, and was known for her careful and steadfast character.

sentences.zh: 述病且卒，主親調飲食，手自奉上，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: When Shu was ill and near death, the princess personally prepared his food and drink and served it with her own hands; the age praised her for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell ill and was near death, the princess personally prepared his food and drink and served it with her own hands; people praised her for this.

sentences.zh: 及宇文化及弑逆，公主隨至聊城，而化及為竇建德所敗，士及自濟北西歸大唐。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, the princess accompanied him to Liaocheng; Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, and Shiji returned west from Jibei to the Great Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, the princess accompanied him to Liaocheng; Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, and Shiji returned west from Jibei to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 時隋代衣冠引見建德，莫不惶懼失常，唯主神色自若。

translations.literal: When the gentry of the Sui court were presented to Jiande, none failed to panic and lose composure—only the princess remained calm and self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: When the gentry of the Sui court were presented to Jiande, none failed to panic and lose composure—only the princess remained calm and self-possessed.

sentences.zh: 建德與語，主自陳國破家亡，不能報怨雪恥，淚上盈襟，聲辭不輟，情理切至。

translations.literal: Jiande spoke with her; the princess declared herself that with the state destroyed and the family ruined she could not avenge her wrongs and wipe away shame; tears brimmed on her collar, her words never ceasing, her reason and feeling utterly earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande spoke with her, and the princess declared that with her state destroyed and her family ruined she could not avenge her wrongs and wipe away her shame; tears brimmed on her collar, her words never ceased, and her reasoning was utterly earnest.

sentences.zh: 建德及觀聽者，莫不為之動容隕涕，咸敬異焉。

translations.literal: Jiande and all who looked on were moved to tears; all admired and marveled at her.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande and all who looked on were moved to tears; everyone admired and marveled at her.

sentences.zh: 及建德誅化及，時主有一子名禪師，年且十歲。

translations.literal: When Jiande executed Huaji, the princess then had a son named Chanshi, nearly ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande executed Huaji, the princess had a son named Chanshi who was nearly ten years old.

sentences.zh: 建德遣武賁郎將於士證謂主曰：「宇文化及躬行弑逆，今將族滅其宗。

translations.literal: Jiande sent the martial guard general Yu Shizheng to tell the princess: "Yuwen Huaji personally committed regicide; now his entire clan will be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande sent the martial guard general Yu Shizheng to tell the princess, "Yuwen Huaji personally committed regicide, and now his entire clan is to be exterminated.

sentences.zh: 公主之子，法當從坐，若不能割愛，亦聽留之。」

translations.literal: The princess's son, by law, should suffer punishment along with them; if you cannot cut your love, you may also keep him."
translations.idiomatic: Your son, by law, ought to share their punishment; if you cannot bring yourself to part with him, you may keep him.

sentences.zh: 主泣曰：「武賁既是隋室貴臣，此事何須見問？」

translations.literal: The princess wept and said: "As a martial guard you are a distinguished minister of the Sui house—why need you ask me about this matter?"
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept and said, "As a martial guard you are a distinguished minister of the Sui house—why need you ask me about a matter like this?"

sentences.zh: 建德竟殺之。

translations.literal: Jiande ultimately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande killed the boy in the end.

sentences.zh: 公主尋請建德，剃髮為尼。

translations.literal: Before long the princess asked Jiande's permission and had her head shaved to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the princess asked Jiande's permission and had her head shaved to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，將歸西京，復與士及遇於東都。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated and she was about to return to the Western Capital, she again encountered Shiji at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande was defeated and she was about to return to the Western Capital, she again encountered Shiji at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 主不與相見。

translations.literal: The princess refused to meet with him.
translations.idiomatic: The princess refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 士及就之，請復為夫妻。

translations.literal: Shiji went to her and asked to become husband and wife again.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji went to her and asked to resume their marriage.

sentences.zh: 主拒曰：「我與君仇家，今恨不能手刃君者，以謀逆之際，君不預知耳。」

translations.literal: The princess refused: "I and your family are enemies; the only reason I do not hate that I cannot personally slay you is that at the time of the plot you did not know of it."
translations.idiomatic: The princess refused and said, "Your family and mine are enemies. The only reason I do not regret that I cannot kill you with my own hand is that you did not know of the plot when it was made.

sentences.zh: 固與告絕。

translations.literal: She firmly broke off with him.
translations.idiomatic: She firmly broke off all relations with him.

sentences.zh: 士及固請，主怒曰：「必就死，可相見也！」

translations.literal: Shiji pressed hard; the princess raged: "Only if you are about to die may you see me!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiji pressed her again, and the princess raged, "Only if you are about to die may you see me!

sentences.zh: 士及知不可屈，乃拜辭而去。

translations.literal: Shiji knew she could not be bent and bowed in farewell and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji knew she could not be moved, bowed in farewell, and left.

sentences.zh: 襄城王恪妃者，循州刺史柳旦女也。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Xiangcheng Ke was the daughter of Liu Dan, Prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Prince Xiangcheng Ke was the daughter of Liu Dan, Prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 妃姿貌端麗，年十餘，以良家子合相，見聘為妃。

translations.literal: The consort's appearance was elegant and beautiful; in her teens, as a daughter of a good family whose physiognomy matched, she was betrothed as consort.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was elegant and beautiful in appearance; in her teens, as a daughter of a good family whose features were deemed auspicious, she was chosen and betrothed as consort.

sentences.zh: 未幾而恪被廢，妃修婦道，事之愈敬。

translations.literal: Before long Ke was deposed; the consort observed the wife's way and served him with still greater respect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ke was deposed, but the consort observed a wife's duties and served him with even greater respect.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，復徙邊，帝令使者殺之於道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Ke was again banished to the frontier; the Emperor ordered an envoy to kill him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Ke was again banished to the frontier, and the Emperor ordered an envoy to kill him on the road.

sentences.zh: 恪與辭決，妃曰：「若王死，妾誓不獨生。」

translations.literal: Ke took leave of her; the consort said: "If the prince dies, your servant vows not to live alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ke took his leave of her, and the consort said, "If the prince dies, I vow not to live alone.

sentences.zh: 於是相對慟哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon they wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: They then wept together face to face.

sentences.zh: 恪死，棺斂訖，妃謂使者曰：「妾誓與楊氏同穴，若身死得不別埋，君之惠也。」

translations.literal: After Ke died and the coffin was prepared, the consort told the envoy: "Your servant vowed to share a grave with the Yang clan; if when I die I may not be buried separately, that will be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: After Ke died and the coffin had been prepared, the consort told the envoy, "I vowed to share a grave with the Yang clan. If when I die I am not buried separately, that will be your kindness.

sentences.zh: 遂撫棺號慟，自經而卒。

translations.literal: She then stroked the coffin wailing, and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She then stroked the coffin and wailed in grief, and hanged herself to death.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不流涕。

translations.literal: All who saw it shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it shed tears.

sentences.zh: 華陽王楷妃者，黃門侍郎、龍涸縣公河南元岩女也。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Huayang Kai was the daughter of Yuan Yan of Henan, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Longhu County.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Prince Huayang Kai was the daughter of Yuan Yan of Henan, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Longhu County.

sentences.zh: 岩明敏有器幹，煬帝嗣位，坐與柳述連事，除外徙南海。

translations.literal: Yan was bright and quick with talent and capacity; when Emperor Yang succeeded, he was punished for association with Liu Shu, removed from office and banished to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was bright and capable; when Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was punished for his association with Liu Shu, removed from office, and exiled to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 後會赦還長安，有人譖岩逃歸，收殺之。

translations.literal: Later, when an amnesty allowed return to Chang'an, someone slandered Yan as having fled back; he was arrested and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an amnesty allowed him to return to Chang'an, someone slandered him as having fled back without permission; he was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 妃有姿色，性婉順，初以選為妃，未幾而楷被幽廢。

translations.literal: The consort had beauty and a gentle, obedient nature; at first chosen as consort, before long Kai was imprisoned and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was beautiful and gentle in temperament; she was first chosen as consort, but before long Kai was imprisoned and deposed.

sentences.zh: 妃事楷愈謹，每見楷有憂懼色，輒陳義理以慰諭之，楷甚敬焉。

translations.literal: The consort served Kai with still greater care; whenever she saw worry and fear on his face, she would set forth principle to comfort and instruct him, and Kai held her in great respect.
translations.idiomatic: The consort served Kai with even greater care; whenever she saw worry and fear on his face, she would set forth moral principle to comfort and instruct him, and Kai held her in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 及江都之亂，楷遇害，宇文化及以妃賜其党元武達。

translations.literal: At the disorder of Jiangdu, Kai met disaster; Yuwen Huaji gave the consort as reward to his follower Yuan Wuda.
translations.idiomatic: At the upheaval at Jiangdu, Kai was killed; Yuwen Huaji gave the consort as a reward to his follower Yuan Wuda.

sentences.zh: 初以宗族禮之，置之別舍。

translations.literal: At first he treated her with clan courtesy and housed her in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: At first he treated her with the courtesy due a clanswoman and housed her in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 後因醉而逼之，妃自誓不屈。

translations.literal: Later, drunk, he forced himself on her; the consort vowed she would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while drunk, he forced himself on her, but the consort vowed she would not yield.

sentences.zh: 武達怒，撻之百餘，詞色彌厲。

translations.literal: Wuda raged and flogged her more than a hundred times; her words and bearing grew fiercer still.
